The exclusivity property is defeated by moving the payload one level down into the Offer. enforce_hook_provenance inspects only the flat iterable it is handed; nothing in the branch binds Offer.discount.value to a granted authorized_discount_pct claim, and Offer.commitments (typed list[Claim]) is walked by neither the guard nor contracts.boundary._claim_provenance_reasons, which iterates bid.claims alone. tools.py:18 asserts 'authorize_discount is the only way a discount reaches an offer' — no code enforces that.

Every runtime capability the branch adds is unwired: ToolHooks and its six hooks, start_bid, would_authorize, Denied, HookCall, HookInputError, enforce_hook_provenance, ClaimScopeError, mint_claim, mint_provenance, claim_fingerprint, scoped_ref, claim_scope, claim_is_scoped_to. Zero production call sites — only the package's own re-exports, its unit tests, and the frozen acceptance suite. packages/store-agent/tests/test_hooks.py states the guard is 'the same function the hosted bid boundary calls'; no such boundary exists anywhere in the repo.

refresh_digests() re-pins approval.content_hash onto whatever the manifest body currently says while leaving approver / approved_at / artifact populated. This defeats the exact tamper-evidence property the frozen acceptance test claims for itself (test_e8_proofs.py:288-291: 'the manifest ... cannot drift after approval without this assertion turning red'). After a re-pin the approval block is fully populated and self-consistent, so the acceptance test goes green again and no reader can tell that a named human's approval now covers bytes they never saw. The CLI warns in prose that 'any approval recorded against the old pins is void', but nothing makes it void in the artifact; --yes skips the prompt entirely, and the library function has no prompt at all.

build_buckets is a pure, deterministic function of the account with no k-anonymity floor, suppression, or generalisation of any kind, so a rotated pseudonym publishes a byte-identical bucket tuple and every rotation is re-linkable. The brief's premise that a floor exists and is measured against a 30-account fixture is false: no such code exists anywhere in the branch or the current tree.

identity_leaks holds every slug of the account's OWN order categories out of the searchable haystack (_incidental_bucket_values, line 383), account-wide rather than per-bucket. category_affinity is the one bucket with no vocabulary or length cap (coarsen_categories, line 215, caps count only at CATEGORY_LIMIT=3), so the buyer's name, street and postal code can be published verbatim into the store-facing profile while the R5 backstop reports clean. The hardening commit's claim that 'everything else is still matched in full' does not hold for this bucket.

AccountDirectory has exactly one implementation and no production populator. build_auth_service() never passes accounts=, so production runs the empty default InMemoryAccountDirectory, and MagicLinkAuth.redeem (line 304) writes only {'email': email} (+orders: []). Every coarsener therefore runs on an empty account in production: GET /buyer/profile returns an identical, information-free profile for every buyer. The passing acceptance test injects a rich account dict straight into build_profile and is not evidence that any production path builds a real profile.

The magic-link token is delivered to the default no-op `_drop` (line 166) in every deployment, and set_auth_service (routes.py:146) — the documented seam for installing a mail transport before the first request — has ZERO callers anywhere in the repository, including tests, which override the FastAPI dependency instead. No production code path can deliver a login link, so magic-link login cannot complete outside a test that injects deliver= itself.

publish_profile — the only writer of app.buyer_accounts, described as 'the store-visible working set' — has zero production call sites, and no code outside the buyer service consumes BuyerProfile or reads app.buyer_accounts. The R5 deliverable 'the BuyerProfile handed to stores' is never handed to a store: GET /buyer/profile requires an X-Buyer-Session header, which only the buyer holds. The hardening commit names publish_profile as dead code but its fix wires only PostgresPseudonymStore, leaving publish_profile dead.

A replayer can relabel a signed delivery onto a topic of its choice AND destroy the genuine one. handle_delivery takes the topic from the UNSIGNED URL path when the X-Shopify-Topic header is absent (`topic = topic or wanted`), while WebhookInbox de-duplicates on the body digest alone (webhooks.py:223-238). The class docstring explicitly raises this exact threat -- 'one captured signed body replay as three distinct fresh events -- a paid order becoming a fabricated fulfilment and a fabricated refund' -- and claims the body-only key defeats it. It defeats the three-events variant only. The one-event-relabelled variant works, and it is worse than a duplicate: it consumes the identity, so the real delivery is swallowed.

merchant-svc has no deployable. The compose fragment this file's own header declares 'Owner: T-050' is still `services: {}`, and nothing anywhere in the repo starts merchant_svc.main:app. Every route, guard and signature check this branch adds therefore has zero production call site in the deployed system -- they exist only under pytest and vitest.

R10's "hard timeout" is measured from the moment solicit_bids constructs its ArrivalClock, not from the auction's own deadline. ArrivalClock's origin is monotonic() at line 181 and its frame start is `now - window`, so the fan-out always gets a FULL `window` of real seconds no matter how much of the window the route already spent on machine.create/open, the ledger write and the per-store eligibility reads (routes.py:169-193 computes `deadline = opened_at + window` BEFORE all of that). Gate latency is therefore free time, and because collect_bids enforces the close on that same shifted stamp, a bid that lands after the auction's stored record.deadline is stamped on time and wins as a non-fallback bid. The route already has a `clock=` parameter it could anchor to opened_at and does not use it.

The hard timeout is bought by abandoning the ThreadPoolExecutor (`shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True)` instead of a `with` block), but a fresh pool is created per request and the abandoned workers are non-daemon threads that survive the response. Threads accumulate without bound for as long as the stores hang, and concurrent.futures' atexit `_python_exit` joins every one of them, so a SIGTERM/graceful shutdown of the exchange blocks on the slowest hung store. sequential_fan_out (fanout.py:239-248) has the same shape. The module docstring reasons only about the abandoned RESULTS ("appends to a list nobody reads again") and never about the abandoned threads.

T-036 — the whole second half of this lane — is unwired. Nothing outside apps/exchange/src/checkout/ ever resolves a provider or calls CheckoutProvider.checkout: the port, both providers, the registry, the domain guard, mint_code and the minting lint have zero production consumers. apps/exchange/src/accept/__init__.py, which T-036's own ticket says is the path that must go through the port, is a 0-byte file. And the frozen suite carries no @pytest.mark.ticket("T-036") test at all, so T-036 contributes 0 of the epic's 3 passes — its 654-line unit-test file is the only thing that has ever executed it.

`configure_auctions` — the only way to give the exchange a real solicitor, a real eligibility source, a Redis-backed store or a real ledger sink — has no production caller anywhere in the repo. The service as it actually boots (`uvicorn exchange.main:app`) therefore runs on _eligibility()'s fail-closed default, StaticSellerEligibility() with no rows, whose answer for every store is UNAVAILABLE. The shipped exchange denies every store and represents none, which is the exact inverse of the R10 property the branch is claimed to deliver; it also silently runs on InMemoryAuctionStore and an InMemoryLedgerSink that is discarded per process, so the DESIGN-pinned `auction:{id}` Redis record with its 15-minute TTL and the ledger trail are never written by any deployment.

A connection failure never becomes a StoreUnavailable, so an unreachable or restarting Postgres returns HTTP 500 with an empty body after a 30-second block, instead of the 503 store_unavailable the module documents. `_connection()` obtains the connection OUTSIDE the try/except in `_append_on`, and `classify_write_error` (pg.py:91) only maps psycopg.errors raised by the INSERT itself. `psycopg_pool.PoolTimeout` and `psycopg.OperationalError` are not EventServiceError subclasses, so `routes._refuse` (routes.py:98) never sees them and the handler raises. Only the no-DSN path reaches StoreUnavailable. errors.py:83 promises '503 - nothing is wrong with the request' and routes.py:216 argues that /events/verify must always answer because 'a 5xx here would be indistinguishable from the verifier being down - which is precisely the state an attacker who had just tampered with the ledger would like it to be confused with'. A down database produces exactly that confusion. The 30 s block is psycopg_pool's default timeout, so with Starlette's 40-thread sync pool ~40 concurrent requests wedge the whole trust service. No test covers it: the only 503 assertion in the 87-test suite is the scorer-unavailable one at test_events.py:1174.

The ledger writer has zero producers. Nothing in the repository writes an event into it - not by import, not over HTTP. A repo-wide grep for `trust.events` / `apps.trust.src.events` / `/events` outside the package returns only the frozen acceptance suite, the branch's own tests, and `trust.main`'s router glob; codegraph agrees. The component that should be the first producer, the exchange auction state machine, emits into `InMemoryLedgerSink`, which its own module docstring (line 8) describes as 'the trust API stub' that 'the default service wiring use[s]'. So the once-only landing, hash chaining and replay this branch built grade an event stream that no part of ProxyShop ever produces. T-060's code is not defective; it is unfed, which is why E6 sits at 2/26 and the four remaining ticket families (T-061 reconcile, T-062 scoring, T-063 feedback, T-065 verification) all fail on ImportError against empty stubs rather than on ledger behaviour.

Ledger writes silently use the wrong DB ROLE. DEFAULT_DSN_ENV = ('PROXYSHOP_LEDGER_DSN','PROXYSHOP_PG_DSN_APP') never consults PROXYSHOP_PG_DSN_TRUST_RW, so a deployment that sets only the documented per-role variable writes the ledger as the 'app' role instead of the 'trust_rw' role D5 grants it. Privilege confusion that no test sees because tests never set the per-role variable. Found by running the real container, not by reading code.

The hardened R8 boundary is not called by anything. enforce_bid_provenance(bid, hooks) must be invoked on the WHOLE bid; passing bid.claims (the flat list) leaves the Offer -- and its discount and stated price -- entirely outside the boundary, which is the original defect. No function can detect this about its own caller. src/runtime/ is empty, so T-041 owns the call site.

A bid's stated price is not reconciled against its granted discount. The floor wall exists, but unit_price ~= list_price * (1 - pct) is NOT verified. A real Bid with an honest 20% grant and unit_price=1.00 under a 10.00 floor was admitted before the floor wall; the arithmetic relation is still unchecked because quantity/currency semantics for total_price are undecided. contracts.boundary.validate_bid does schema + provenance + expiry + eligibility but NO price/floor reconciliation, which is why this was invisible everywhere.

EVENTS_ROLE = "app", and its comment asserts app is 'the role the writer connects as... deliberately not trust_rw'. That statement is now false: compose, .env.example, proxyshop_support.postgres.ROLES and the T-151 fix all say the shipped ledger writer is trust_rw. Consequence: every DB-backed test in apps/trust exercises a database principal the deployment does not use, against a DIFFERENT grant set (app has SELECT+INSERT on ledger plus full DML on app and sealed; trust_rw has full DML on ledger, read-only on app, nothing in sealed). The suite's DB coverage is therefore evidence about the wrong role.

MAX_SWEEP_DEPTH = 12 truncates the provenance walk SILENTLY. A priced node, a claim, or a discount nested 13+ levels deep in a dict-shaped bid is admitted having been inspected by nothing. This bypasses EVERY boundary wall — the claim provenance walk, the floor wall and the new price reconciliation alike — not merely the price checks, so it is strictly wider than the T-153 defect that surfaced it. Raising the bound does not fix it, and refusing everything past the bound would refuse an honestly deep metadata blob, which _sweep is explicitly written to tolerate. The bound's stated purpose is to stop a self-referential dict hanging the boundary, so the correct fix is CYCLE DETECTION replacing the depth bound.

offer.total_price is never reconciled against unit_price: an offer stating unit_price=80.0 with total_price=1.0 is admitted. Offer carries no quantity, and the quantity that would relate the two lives in apps/exchange/src/checkout/codes.py:111, so the relation is not decidable from a bid alone. The T-153 lane scoped this out explicitly and documented it in the refusal's docstring rather than leaving it silent. Closing it requires deciding where quantity enters the bid — a design question, not a bug fix.

An off-domain permalink from a delegating merchant client leaves a LIVE single-use discount code with no ledger record. The offer's checkout_url is checked BEFORE the mint, but an offer with NO url — the legal R10 list-price fallback shape that collect_bids manufactures — gives that check nothing to look at. The first failable host comparison is therefore the one on the permalink returned BY mint, i.e. AFTER POST /codes has already issued a real discount code. Measured on task/T-033: merchant invoked once, code PSX-REALCODE live, accept correctly returns no permalink and leaves the auction open, and NO code_created event exists for that code. Carrying the minted code out on OffDomainCheckout so the exchange can revoke it is T-036's file.

The one-accept-per-auction guard is only as durable as the record handed in. accept() stamps the auction OBJECT it receives. A route that loads an AuctionRecord from RedisAuctionStore, accepts, and does not save it back leaves an unstamped record for the next request; and two concurrent requests reading it can both pass the guard, because the check-then-act window spans the whole provider call including merchant I/O. The durable guard belongs on AuctionStateMachine's already-serialised ACCEPTED transition.

SYSTEMIC GATE-CREDIBILITY DEFECT: tests that swallow a missing subject with `except ImportError` are VACUOUS until the subject exists, and report green the whole time. test_checkout_provider.py:406 counted accept()'s no-default positionals but was wrapped so it tolerated accept not existing at all — it had therefore NEVER run for real until T-033 created the module, at which point it immediately went red. This is the third vacuous gate found in cycle 10 alone: red-check independently proved T-111's and T-123's gates EXIT 0 with their defects live. The class is 'a gate that cannot fail is indistinguishable from a gate that passes', and it is what let earlier waves report T-109/T-111/T-123 fixed when git says the files were never touched. Needs a repo-wide sweep for except-ImportError-tolerant tests and skip/xfail guards whose condition is permanently true.

These three tickets' recorded `verify` commands pass IDENTICALLY with and without their defect, which is the precise mechanism by which all three were reported closed twice while the defects stayed live. red-check measured it this cycle: T-111's `./scripts/bootstrap.sh && ./scripts/verify.sh check` and T-123's `bootstrap.sh && pytest packages/llm && python -c 'import contracts, llm, trust'` both exit 0 with nothing implemented (3046 and 210 tests selected), and T-109's `pytest apps/trust -q && pytest proxyshop_support -q` was green on the parent commit. The lane has now written real gates; the graph's verify strings should be repaired to point at them.

T-033's registered-domain guard is DECORATIVE in the deployed configuration. `_platform_domains` is module state initialised to None and NOTHING in the repository calls `use_registered_domains`, so under `uvicorn exchange.main:app` the resolution yields None, CheckoutRequest(registered_domains=None) is built, and registered_domain_for falls back to `bid['store_domain']` — a field the bidder controls. The frozen S8-3 blocker test_offdomain_checkout_url_is_refused therefore PASSES on that decorative comparison, which means spec_criteria_passing counts a decorative pass toward its target. Worse, the package's own wiring docstring tells an integrator to wire `apps.exchange.src.accept`, while the served app reads `exchange.accept` — measured as the SAME FILE (equal inode) but DIFFERENT module objects, so wiring one spelling leaves the other completely unwired and an accept through the unwired spelling mints a real single-use discount code for a host the platform never registered. apps/trust/src/ledger/__init__.py and packages/store-agent/src/hooks/__init__.py both already implement _install_canonical_alias() for exactly this hazard; the accept package skipped that convention.

There is no HTTP path by which a buyer's accept can reach accept() or accept_offer(). The accept half is complete, tested and lint-enforced, but has no production consumer and no wiring — so no deployed path is protected by any of it.

The D37 Neo4j lock is MACHINE-GLOBAL (/private/tmp/proxyshop-neo4j.lock) and PROXYSHOP_WORKER does not isolate it, so it is shared across every worktree and every concurrent lane. Its own 600s wait is UNREACHABLE by construction because the repo-wide addopts carry --timeout=300: under contention the session-scoped _neo4j_guard fixture dies inside time.sleep(poll) with 'Failed: Timeout (>300.0s) from pytest-timeout' instead of the diagnosable Neo4jLockTimeout the module exists to raise. This is a swarm-scale hazard: it turns lock contention into an undiagnosable red that looks like a product failure.

The tests that spin their OWN fresh-volume Postgres container use no shared fixture and so land in the fallback. FIVE of the eight are the schema-grants/role-password security tests in apps/trust/tests/test_schema_grants.py and proxyshop_support/tests/test_role_password_end_to_end.py — the same class of security check whose silent skipping the ticket was written to stop. One instance was reintroduced by this very merge: apps/trust/tests/test_events_hardening.py:146 (T-151's own new test) points at a CLOSED loopback port and needs no datastore at all, yet is classified whole-stack.

A REMOVED LINE IN THIS BATCH TURNED A LOUD FAILURE INTO A SILENT FAIL-OPEN, and the per-branch removed-lines audit cleared it as benign. The batch replaced `list_price = float(listing.get("list_price") or 0.0)` with `list_price = self.list_price(product_ref) or 0.0`. The new list_price() swallows TypeError/ValueError and returns None for a catalog entry whose list_price is not a number; the `or 0.0` at the call site then coerces that None into a real number. So a malformed catalog entry that previously raised now silently prices at 0.0 inside the discount evaluator — the exact class of defect T-153 was created to close, relocated into the code that closes it. Only visible on the combined diff, which is why rung 2 exists.

test_the_flat_namespaces_survive_a_pytest_run runs `chflags -R hidden` on the checkout's REAL shared .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages — the one piece of state PROXYSHOP_WORKER cannot isolate — then runs a nested pytest with a 600s timeout before restoring it in a finally. For that entire window every other Python process starting in this checkout loses the .pkgroot namespaces and fails with ModuleNotFoundError. That breaks any concurrently running service, `make demo-seed`, a sibling lane, OR A METRIC MEASUREMENT. This is a live hazard to the swarm and to the frozen build_succeeds metric, which has already recorded four false zeros in six cycles.

Neither the new price-reconciliation wall nor the pre-existing floor wall looks at Offer.total_price (PRICE_FIELD == 'unit_price'), so a bid can state a fully honest unit_price and an arbitrary total_price and be admitted — the same unauthorised-discount shape T-153 closed, moved one field over. DESIGN.md:127 specifies the ranking price dimension as a function of total_price, and the C11 accepted-event payload records total_price verbatim, so a downstream consumer can treat an unreconciled number as authoritative. Companion to T-156 with the design citation attached.

ORCHESTRATOR ADJUDICATION of the T-169/T-170 vs refuted-zero-callers contradiction, recorded so it cannot be re-litigated. NO ticket in the 123-ticket graph owns an accept HTTP route: T-033's scope is apps/exchange/src/accept/** but its frozen tests grade the LIBRARY (accept() called directly, no TestClient anywhere in the acceptance suite), and T-052's scope is apps/merchant/svc/src/codes/** — the Shopify adapter, not the exchange route. So T-170 is DOWNGRADED from HIGH to this graph gap: it is the ordinary zero-caller pattern (unfinished work awaiting a schedule), not a defect. T-169 is NOT downgraded and stands as HIGH, because it fails the discriminator: the frozen S8-3 release blocker PASSES today by comparing the permalink host against bid['store_domain'], a BIDDER-CONTROLLED field, since no registry is ever wired — so spec_criteria_passing counts a security property as met that a consistently-lying bidder defeats. The rule: an unwired half is scheduled work; it becomes a defect the moment a frozen test counts it as satisfying a requirement.

T-153'S WALL IS ON THE WRONG DOOR AND THE ORIGINAL ATTACK STILL WORKS END TO END. Measured by the sabotage lens against the CLEAN tree, through the real dual-path bid door the acceptance harness uses: a hosted bid carrying a genuine hook-minted 20% grant, declaring 20%, charging 15.00 on a product listed at 100.00 -> validate_bid returns ok=True, reasons=[]. The price reconciliation lives only in the store-agent's enforce_bid_provenance, which is the EMITTING side; contracts.boundary — the VALIDATING side, and the only boundary the exchange can run — contains no reference to enforce_bid_provenance, list_price or reconciliation at all. So the wall protects only bids produced by our own runtime, and a store that does not run our runtime bypasses it entirely. Corroborated: the S1d witness counted 49 lines in a store-agent-only run and 49 in the full-suite run, identical, so nothing outside packages/store-agent/tests exercises that code. NOTE T-041 (accepted this cycle, not yet merged) adds the first production caller on the emitting side; it does NOT close this, because the validating side is untouched.

BID-WIDE PRICE RECONCILIATION PASSES A FULL GREEN SUITE. Sabotage S1d replaced the per-offer lookup `declared.get(node, 0.0)` with `max(declared.values(), default=0.0)` — i.e. one grant licenses every priced node in the bid — and NOTHING CAUGHT IT: package 111 passed, full suite 3368 passed, 1 skipped, with a 49-line witness proving the mutated bytecode executed. Measured escape: one 20% grant, `.offer` at 80.00 declaring 20%, `.bundled` at 80.00 declaring NOTHING -> sabotaged ADMITTED, clean REFUSED. ENVELOPE VERSION HISTORY IS PROCESS-LOCAL AND DIES WITH THE PROCESS.
